key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings achieve better long-term corrosion and wear performance when spray conditions produce disk-like droplets, dense lamellar microstructures, and low porosity.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spraying parameters to minimize defects can improve durability of steel components exposed to humid environments and combined corrosion-wear service.
method: Detonation spray Fe-based amorphous coatings onto Q235 carbon steel under varied process parameters.
Characterize droplet morphology and coating microstructure, including circularity, expansion factor, and porosity.
Evaluate long-term corrosion behavior and tribological performance under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic corrosion and tribology testing and links higher porosity to poorer corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity lowers friction coefficient and wear rate.
watch_item: Results may depend strongly on spray parameter control and humidity environment, so performance should not be assumed without matching service conditions.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
